title: Wolf and Garden Anew
premise: Xanthe Whitlock, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, has hidden her gift for twelve years in Vellharrow, a city where magic is outlawed and informants are paid in bread. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin receiving answers, every answered prayer leaves a bone-white mark on Xanthe's carvings — proof that the gods are using her as a conduit without her consent. Hunted by the Inquisitor's Wardens and courted by a wolf-god who claims she alone can decide whether the old gods return or die forever, Xanthe must carry the secret of her own divine parentage: she is the last living anchor binding the gods out of the world, and if she speaks it aloud before the thirteenth moon turns, the seal breaks and war reignites. In the end, Xanthe refuses both silence and sacrifice, carving her own name into the ancient seal so that the gods may return only by her invitation — choosing found family and love over duty to either side.
about_author: Sebastian Sandoval is a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring medieval reliquaries before turning to fiction full-time. He writes fantasy about craft, faith, and the people history forgets, from a farmhouse full of rescued animals.

chapters.title: The Quiet Trade
chapters.summary: Xanthe carves a mourning charm for a grieving widow, hearing the dead grandmother's last words through the bone. POV: Xanthe. Establishes her secret gift, her poverty, and the city's fear of magic; ends when the widow's prayer to a dead god is somehow answered, leaving a white mark on the charm.

chapters.title: Marks on Bone
chapters.summary: Xanthe investigates the mark, finding three more on charms sold across the city, each tied to an answered prayer. POV: Xanthe. Rising unease and curiosity; she realizes the marks appear only on her work, meaning something vast has noticed her specifically.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Halvard Reeve, a Warden who once spared her as a child, arrives investigating the answered prayers. POV: alternating Xanthe and Reeve. Cat-and-mouse tension; Reeve suspects her but owes her a debt, buying her time at a terrible price: she must report anything she learns.

chapters.title: The Wolf at the Threshold
chapters.summary: A great grey wolf appears in Xanthe's workshop, speaking with the voice of Veyran, god of thresholds and debts. POV: Xanthe. Awe and terror; Veyran claims the other gods are waking and that she is the door they are knocking on, though he won't say why.

chapters.title: Found Kin
chapters.summary: Xanthe shelters with her chosen family: Tam, a defrocked priest turned smuggler, and Odile, a hedge-witch healer. POV: Tam. Warmth and banter ground the story; Tam recognizes Veyran's name from forbidden texts and warns that gods always collect their debts in blood.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Xanthe questions the dead through old bones, learning the gods were sealed away not by villains but by their own mortal children after a catastrophic war. POV: Xanthe. Grief and moral complexity; the seal was mercy, and someone or something is now unmaking it.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Veyran reveals the deadline: the seal weakens each lunar cycle and fails entirely at the thirteenth turn unless re-forged. POV: Reeve. The Warden's own crisis of faith deepens as his prayers go unanswered while beggars' are granted; he begins doubting the church he serves.

chapters.title: A Debt in Silver
chapters.summary: Veyran offers Xanthe protection for her family in exchange for carrying his message to the other waking gods. POV: Xanthe. Temptation and resentment; she accepts because refusing means Tam and Odile become targets, hating that love makes her pliable.

chapters.title: The Pilgrim Road
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Tam travel to the shrine-city of Aurelach, where pilgrims flock to newly answering altars. POV: Tam. Wonder shadowed by dread; they witness a miracle heal a child and a rival miracle burn a skeptic alive, showing the gods' return cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Sister of the Seal
chapters.summary: At Aurelach, high priestess Maren Corvane recognizes the white marks and names Xanthe 'Anchor' — the living linchpin of the seal. POV: Xanthe. Shock and denial; Maren explains the Anchors were bred for the purpose, and Xanthe's parents died hiding what she is.

chapters.title: The God Who Lies Kindly
chapters.summary: Veyran admits he woke the others early, gambling that a willing Anchor could reshape the seal rather than merely maintain it. POV: Xanthe. Betrayal and fury; she realizes she has been a piece on his board since chapter one, yet part of her understands his desperation.

chapters.title: Wardens Descend
chapters.summary: Reeve leads a Warden purge on Aurelach, ordered to execute the Anchor if she cannot be contained. POV: Reeve. Moral fracture; he finds Xanthe and instead of arresting her, gives her a head start, formally becoming a traitor to his order.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Shrine
chapters.summary: Fleeing the burning shrine-city, the group loses Odile, captured by Wardens as leverage. POV: Xanthe. Despair and guilt; Xanthe wants to surrender herself, but Tam argues the family survives only if she stays free — loyalty pulling against truth.

chapters.title: The Court of Antlers
chapters.summary: Xanthe petitions the waking gods directly at a moonlit crossroads, meeting Sereth, goddess of the hunt, who wants the seal broken and war renewed against humanity. POV: Xanthe. Cold dread; Sereth confirms the truth of her parentage — her mother was the previous Anchor, her father a god who chose mortality.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: With two turns remaining, Maren defects from the church and teaches Xanthe the Anchor rites, which require a willing death. POV: Maren. Solemn intimacy; the old rite assumed the Anchor would die willingly, and Maren believes Xanthe must too — setting up the central choice.

chapters.title: Prisoner Exchange
chapters.summary: Reeve secretly frees Odile, exposing himself to execution, and delivers a message: the Inquisition knows Xanthe is the Anchor and plans to kill her at the twelfth turn to force the seal's collapse and end magic permanently. POV: Reeve. Sacrifice and resolve; he chooses truth over the institution that made him.

chapters.title: The Wolf's Confession
chapters.summary: Veyran confesses the deeper secret: the original war began because the gods demanded worship as tribute, and the seal was humanity's refusal — but Veyran alone opposed the demand, and has spent millennia seeking another way. POV: Xanthe. Compassion rekindled; she stops seeing him as captor and sees a fellow prisoner of duty.

chapters.title: Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: The Inquisition's army marches on the crossroads where the gods gather; Sereth moves to break the seal by killing Xanthe publicly, believing martyrdom will shatter it faster than patience. POV: alternating Xanthe and Reeve. Alliances collide; Tam and Odile rally smugglers and pilgrims to hold the line.

chapters.title: War's Old Face
chapters.summary: Battle erupts between Wardens, pilgrims, and manifesting gods; Reeve dies holding the line so Xanthe can reach the seal-stone. POV: Reeve, ending mid-sacrifice. Grief and fury; his death crystallizes Xanthe's refusal to let anyone — god or human — spend other people like coin.

chapters.title: The Carver's Name
chapters.summary: At the seal-stone under the thirteenth moon, Xanthe rejects both options: not the sacrificial rite, not Sereth's war. She carves her own name into the stone, rewriting the seal so the gods return only by individual invitation, one believer at a time. POV: Xanthe. Transcendence; the power nearly unmakes her until Veyran anchors her with his own diminished divinity.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Moons
chapters.summary: Sereth withdraws to the wild places, bound by the new terms; the surviving gods scatter as small presences, answerable only where invited. POV: Xanthe. Exhausted peace; she buries Reeve, mourns honestly, and faces a world where magic is legal again but no longer compulsory or weaponized.

chapters.title: Wolf and Garden Anew
chapters.summary: One year later, Xanthe reopens her carving shop with Tam and Odile; Veyran, diminished to wolf-shape, takes up residence on her doorstep as companion rather than creditor. POV: Xanthe. Quiet joy; the final image is her carving a garden gate from antler bone, opening it onto a world where faith is a choice freely made.
